units.text: INT. SISTERS - CONTINUOUS
In PROSOROV’S house.
A sitting-room with pillars; behind is seen a large dining-room.
It is midday, the sun is shining brightly outside.
In the dining-room the table is being laid for lunch.

OLGA, in the regulation blue dress of a teacher at a girl’s high school, is walking about correcting exercise books; MASHA, in a black dress, with a hat on her knees, sits and reads a book; IRINA, in white, stands about, with a thoughtful expression.

It’s just a year since father died last May the fifth, on your name-day, Irina. It was very cold then, and snowing. I thought I would never survive it, and you were in a dead faint. And now a year has gone by and we are already thinking about it without pain, and you are wearing a white dress and your face is happy.
units.name: OLGA

units.text: Clock strikes twelve.
And the clock struck just the same way then.
units.name: OLGA

units.text: Pause.

I remember that there was music at the funeral, and they fired a volley in the cemetery. He was a general in command of a brigade but there were few people present. Of course, it was raining then, raining hard, and snowing.
units.name: OLGA

units.text: Why think about it!
units.name: IRINA

units.text: BARON TUZENBACH, CHEBUTIKIN and SOLENI appear by the table in the dining-room, behind the pillars.

It’s so warm to-day that we can keep the windows open, though the birches are not yet in flower. Father was put in command of a brigade, and he rode out of Moscow with us eleven years ago. I remember perfectly that it was early in May and that everything in Moscow was flowering then. It was warm too, everything was bathed in sunshine. Eleven years have gone, and I remember everything as if we rode out only yesterday. Oh, God! When I awoke this morning and saw all the light and the spring, joy entered my heart, and I longed passionately to go home.
units.name: OLGA

units.text: Will you take a bet on it?
units.name: CHEBUTIKIN

units.text: Oh, nonsense.
units.name: TUZENBACH

units.text: MASHA, lost in a reverie over her book, whistles softly.
Don’t whistle, Masha. How can you!
units.name: OLGA

units.text: Pause.

I’m always having headaches from having to go to the High School every day and then teach till evening. Strange thoughts come to me, as if I were already an old woman. And really, during these four years that I have been working here, I have been feeling as if every day my strength and youth have been squeezed out of me, drop by drop. And only one desire grows and gains in strength...
units.name: OLGA

units.text: To go away to Moscow. To sell the house, drop everything here, and go to Moscow...
units.name: IRINA

units.text: Yes! To Moscow, and as soon as possible.
units.name: OLGA

units.text: CHEBUTIKIN and TUZENBACH laugh.
I expect Andrey will become a professor, but still, he won’t want to live here. Only poor Masha must go on living here.
units.name: IRINA

units.text: Masha can come to Moscow every year, for the whole summer.
units.name: OLGA

units.text: MASHA is whistling gently.
Everything will be arranged, please God.
units.name: IRINA

units.text: Looks out of the window.

It’s nice out to-day. I don’t know why I’m so happy: I remembered this morning that it was my name-day, and I suddenly felt glad and remembered my childhood, when mother was still with us. What beautiful thoughts I had, what thoughts!
units.name: IRINA

units.text: You’re all radiance to-day, I’ve never seen you look so lovely. And Masha is pretty, too. Andrey wouldn’t be bad-looking, if he wasn’t so stout; it does spoil his appearance. But I’ve grown old and very thin, I suppose it’s because I get angry with the girls at school. To-day I’m free. I’m at home. I haven’t got a headache, and I feel younger than I was yesterday. I’m only twenty-eight.... All’s well, God is everywhere, but it seems to me that if only I were married and could stay at home all day, it would be even better.
units.name: OLGA

units.text: Pause.
I should love my husband.
units.name: OLGA

units.text: To SOLENI.
I’m tired of listening to the rot you talk.
units.name: TUZENBACH

units.text: Entering the sitting-room.
I forgot to say that Vershinin, our new lieutenant-colonel of artillery, is coming to see us to-day.
units.name: TUZENBACH

units.text: Sits down to the piano.
That’s good. I’m glad.
units.name: OLGA

units.text: Is he old?
units.name: IRINA

units.text: Oh, no. Forty or forty-five, at the very outside.
units.name: TUZENBACH

units.text: Plays softly.
He seems rather a good sort. He’s certainly no fool, only he likes to hear himself speak.
units.name: TUZENBACH

units.text: Is he interesting?
units.name: IRINA

units.text: Oh, he’s all right, but there’s his wife, his mother-in-law, and two daughters. This is his second wife. He pays calls and tells everybody that he’s got a wife and two daughters. He’ll tell you so here. The wife isn’t all there, she does her hair like a flapper and gushes extremely. She talks philosophy and tries to commit suicide every now and again, apparently in order to annoy her husband. I should have left her long ago, but he bears up patiently, and just grumbles.
units.name: TUZENBACH

units.text: Enters with CHEBUTIKIN from the dining-room.

With one hand I can only lift fifty-four pounds, but with both hands I can lift 180, or even 200 pounds. From this I conclude that two men are not twice as strong as one, but three times, perhaps even more....
units.name: SOLENI

units.text: Reads a newspaper as he walks.
If your hair is coming out... take an ounce of naphthaline and hail a bottle of spirit... dissolve and use daily....
units.name: CHEBUTIKIN

units.text: Makes a note in his pocket diary.
